findings.title: Where report and aggregate queries live
findings.recency: B is newer: reports.ts was last changed 2026-10-09, payments.ts 2026-03-03.
findings.recommendation: Both, with a rule: per-entity reads and writes live in repositories; cross-entity report queries live in src/export/reports.ts, take TenantScope first and guard full rows. This makes the existing read model an explicit exception to the rule in rules.md.
findings.decision: Both, with a rule (25 Oct 2026). Per-entity reads and writes live in src/db/repositories. Cross-entity report queries live in src/export/reports.ts, take TenantScope first and pass full rows through guard(). rules.md names this exception. Removing the dead duplicates (payments.revenueByPeriod, access.allSyncLag) is an optional cleanup ticket.

findings.title: How a server action reports an expected failure
findings.recency: Mixed. Return-style actions date 2026-04 to 2026-08; the throwing session helpers 2026-09-05.
findings.recommendation: A is the standard: return { ok: false, message } for anything a user can cause, including a missing permission. Throw only for states that indicate a programming error.
findings.decision: A is the standard (25 Oct 2026). A server action returns { ok: false, message } for anything a user can cause, including a missing permission or a disabled feature. It throws only for states that mean a bug.

findings.title: How a server action checks who may do it
findings.recency: No clear direction; all three were touched between 2026-08 and 2026-10.
findings.recommendation: A is the standard: every action calls can() or requirePermission with a PERMISSIONS key, including member self-service and staff-only actions. Combine with the C2 answer for whether it returns or throws.
findings.decision: A is the standard (25 Oct 2026). Every server action checks a PERMISSIONS key, including member self-service (self.book, self.subscription) and staff-only actions, and returns { ok: false, message } when the check fails (per C2). Adding a non-throwing check beside requirePermission and replacing assertMay* and isBeefcakeStaff checks are cleanup tickets.

findings.title: How Beefcake staff narrow to one tenant
findings.recommendation: A is the standard. scope.ts is a talk-first file, so this decision only says which existing function to call.
findings.decision: A is the standard (25 Oct 2026). Staff narrow to one tenant with impersonate(admin, tenantId), so the scope keeps the staff actor. Exception: the batch signal export in src/export/signals.ts has no person behind it, so it builds per-tenant scopes the way jobs do, with tenantScope(id, { db, actorRole: 'system' }). The exception covers batch CLIs only, never a page or an action.

findings.title: Where "now" comes from
findings.recency: clock.ts is the oldest (2026-03-24); signals.ts the newest (2026-10-09).
findings.recommendation: A is the standard for request code; CLIs and the runner call the same function. Merging the copies is a cleanup ticket, not part of this decision.
findings.decision: A is the standard (25 Oct 2026). clock() from src/lib/clock.ts is the only source of request time in actions and pages, and of the default now in the CLIs and the job runner. Jobs keep reading now from their context so --now replays, and domain functions take the instant as an argument. Exception: job_runs.finished_at is stamped with the real wall clock, because it records when the process actually finished. Merging defaultNow and seededToday into clock() is a cleanup ticket.

findings.title: How a domain function says "not allowed"
findings.recency: A and C are 2026-08; B is the oldest (2025-10-30).
findings.recommendation: A for a yes/no decision with reasons (a discriminated union on ok). Keep a domain word as the discriminant where it carries meaning (granted/denied for access). B stops being used for new code.
findings.decision: Both A and C, with a rule (25 Oct 2026). A yes/no domain decision with reasons returns a discriminated union on ok. A domain word may be the discriminant where it carries meaning (granted/denied for access). { allowed, reason? } is not used in new code.

findings.title: Which error type a broken invariant throws
findings.recency: B is used for the newest case (ReportTimeoutError, 2026-10-09).
findings.recommendation: Both A and B, with a rule: built-in errors for a bad argument; a named subclass for anything a caller is expected to catch. C is not used.
findings.decision: Both A and B, with a rule (25 Oct 2026). Throw a built-in TypeError or RangeError for a bad argument, and a named Error subclass for anything a caller is expected to catch. A plain Error is not used. Moving proration.ts:91 to CurrencyMismatchError is a cleanup ticket.

findings.title: Where status and enum value lists are defined
findings.recommendation: B is the source: the domain declares an as-const list, and schema.ts imports it for its enum. This changes schema.ts without a migration, but confirm with whoever owns the schema.
findings.decision: B is the source (25 Oct 2026). A value list is declared once in src/domain as an as-const array or union, and src/db/schema.ts imports it for its enum. No migration is needed, because the column type does not change. Adding a ChargeStatus type and switching schema.ts over are cleanup tickets.

findings.title: Turning a database string into a PlainDate
findings.recommendation: Both, with a rule: cast only in a repository mapper, for a column the schema already constrains; assert anything from a user, a URL or a file. Pages stop casting.
findings.decision: Both, with a rule (25 Oct 2026). Cast as PlainDate only inside a repository mapper, for a column the schema constrains. Use assertPlainDate() for anything from a user, a URL or a file. Pages do not cast.

findings.title: Converting instants to and from strings
findings.recommendation: A for writing (.toISOString()); fromIso for parsing strings that did not come from our own columns. toIso can be retired.
findings.decision: Both, with a rule (25 Oct 2026). Write instants with .toISOString(). Parse with fromIso() any string that did not come from one of our own _at columns. toIso is retired (cleanup ticket).

findings.decision: A is the standard (25 Oct 2026). Import repositories as import * as xRepo from '@/db/repositories/x'; named imports from observability are allowed. AGENTS.md is corrected to match. Deleting the unused barrels is a cleanup ticket.

findings.decision: Both, with a rule (25 Oct 2026). src and scripts call databasePath(). tests/e2e and root config files may spell out the env var and default, because e2e imports nothing from src.

findings.title: Where an e2e test gets its data

variants.name: A
variants.summary: Find suitable rows in the seed

variants.name: B
variants.summary: Fixture inserts and removes its own rows

variants.name: C
variants.summary: Create through the UI, no cleanup

findings.recommendation: B for anything that needs a precise state; A is fine for read-only checks. C only when the test is about creating the row, and then it removes it.
findings.decision: All three, with a rule (25 Oct 2026). A test that needs a precise state uses a fixture that inserts its own rows and removes them. Read-only checks may find rows in the seed. A test creates rows through the UI only when creating them is what it tests, and then it removes them.

findings.title: Three generations of e2e files

findings.decision: A and B, with a rule (25 Oct 2026). Tests tied to a BCPLA Spec use the acceptance template. Plan-driven tests with no ticket use the planner layout. Both import expect from ../evidence. The legacy root files stay as they are and are never copied.
